body: **Foco:** Advanced relative clauses — prática e contraste.
**Pronúncia:** Ênfase intencional.
**22 palavras novas** (análises).
**Texto do dia:** texto acadêmico e resumo.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo contrastar relativas restritivas e não restritivas e reduzir relativas em um texto acadêmico.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Abstract: Rivers and Settlement
paras: Settlements **that** grew beside rivers developed faster than those **that** did not. The Nile valley, **where** agriculture first flourished, illustrates this. Cities **founded** on trade routes, **many of which** were rivers, became centers of power. The river Danube, **along which** several capitals stand, is a typical case.

The authors, **whose** earlier study was widely cited, argue that water, **which** supports food, trade and defense, explains much of the pattern. Sources **cited** in the appendix, **the reliability of which** varies, are discussed separately.

items.q: The Nile valley is an example of early agriculture.
The authors’ earlier study was ignored.
All sources cited are equally reliable.

Pontuação
Exemplo
rows: Settlements **that grew beside rivers** developed faster.
The Nile, **which supports farming**, flows north.
Cities **founded on trade routes** (= that were founded)
many of which / some of whom
trade routes, **many of which** were rivers

blocks.body: **That** só em restritivas; **which** em restritivas e não restritivas, mas **com vírgulas** só nas não restritivas. Relativas reduzidas: *cities founded on…* (passiva), *a team studying…* (ativa).
Retire as vírgulas e veja se muda o sentido: se mudar, a oração é restritiva.

items.s: Cities ___ on trade routes became powerful. (found, part.)
The Nile, ___ agriculture first flourished, is a good example. (where)
Trade routes, many ___ which were rivers, mattered. (of)
The Danube, along ___ several capitals stand, is typical. (which)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **a case in point** — um caso exemplar
**which goes to show that…** — o que mostra que…
**where it all began** — onde tudo começou
**the heart of the matter** — o cerne da questão
**a point of reference** — um ponto de referência
**the root of the problem** — a raiz do problema
**a clear pattern emerges** — surge um padrão claro
**as the saying goes** — como diz o ditado
**So commas matter?** — Então as vírgulas importam?
**What is the difference between the two kinds of clause?** — Qual é a diferença entre os dois tipos de oração?
**A defining clause identifies; a non-defining clause adds information.** — A restritiva identifica; a não restritiva acrescenta informação.

blocks.title: Seminar
lines: What is the difference between the two kinds of clause?
Qual é a diferença entre os dois tipos de oração?
A defining clause identifies; a non-defining clause adds information.
A restritiva identifica; a não restritiva acrescenta informação.
Yes. Remove them and see if the meaning changes.
Sim. Retire-as e veja se o sentido muda.

prompts.model: Cities that grew beside rivers prospered.
The Danube, which crosses ten countries, is long.
Cities founded on trade routes grew fast.

blocks.task: Write 6 sentences: two defining, two non-defining, two reduced.
blocks.model: Students who revise regularly succeed. Books that are translated reach more readers. The library, which opened in 1890, is closed today. My brother, who lives in Lisbon, is visiting. Documents stored in the archive are public. Teachers working abroad often change their view.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
